answer: Hardware-attested keys: each agent must sign its work with a key sealed inside a secure chip, and the network accepts only one active identity per attested device. A fake can wander between IP addresses, but its pulse always traces back to the same chip, so a second account on that device simply earns nothing. To field a thousand Sybils, an attacker must buy and power a thousand certified devices, a real capital cost with no safe harbor of cheap virtual copies.
